title: SAT 06 · Number lines and distance
description: A/B reasoning practice. Difficulty is editorial, not standardized SAT calibration.

questions.title: Distance Across Zero
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Two checkpoints are at positions \(-4\) and \(+4\) on a number line. What is the distance between the two checkpoints? Choose A or B and show how you use their positions.
questions.explanation: The checkpoints are at \(-4\) and \(+4\). Their distance is the absolute difference of their positions: \(|4-(-4)|=|8|=8\) units. Adding the signed positions gives \(-4+4=0\), but that sum is not the distance between the points. Therefore, choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Count the units from one checkpoint to zero and from zero to the other, or subtract the coordinates and take the absolute value.

questions.title: Temperature Gap on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: At sunrise, the temperature is \(-6^\circ\text{C}\). By noon, it is \(+3^\circ\text{C}\). How many degrees did the temperature change? Choose A or B and use the number-line positions to justify your answer.
questions.explanation: The change is the distance between the readings, \(|3-(-6)|=|9|=9^\circ\text{C}\). The value \(3^\circ\text{C}\) is the final temperature, not the amount of change. Therefore, choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: Two temperature readings are marked on a horizontal number line at minus 6 degrees Celsius and plus 3 degrees Celsius; the distance between them is 9 degrees.

questions.hint: Find how far apart the two readings are on the number line; the final temperature itself is not the change.

questions.title: Which Point Is Farther from Zero?
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Point \(P\) is at \(-5\) and point \(Q\) is at \(+7\) on a number line. Which point is farther from zero? Choose A or B and use absolute values in your explanation.
questions.explanation: Distance from zero is the absolute value of a position. Point \(P\) is \(|-5|=5\) units from zero, while point \(Q\) is \(|7|=7\) units from zero. Since \(7>5\), point \(Q\) is farther away. A smaller signed coordinate does not necessarily mean a greater distance from zero, so choice A is incorrect.

visuals.alt: A table lists point P at minus 5 and point Q at plus 7 on a number line.

questions.hint: Distance from zero ignores the sign; compare the absolute values of the two positions.

questions.title: Moving Left from a Positive Position
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A token starts at \(+2\) on a number line and moves \(5\) units to the left. Where does it finish? Choose A or B and explain how the direction of movement changes the coordinate.
questions.explanation: Moving left means subtracting from the starting coordinate, so the final position is \(2-5=-3\). The token passes zero and ends three units to its left. Choice B results from using the distance \(5-2=3\) without preserving the direction, so choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Moving left decreases the coordinate; start at +2 and count 5 units in that direction, past zero if necessary.

questions.title: Points Six Units from a Negative Center
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A point \(x\) is exactly \(6\) units from \(-2\) on a number line. Which pair lists all possible values of \(x\)? Choose A or B and show how the two directions from \(-2\) are represented.
questions.explanation: Being 6 units from \(-2\) means \(|x-(-2)|=6\), or \(|x+2|=6\). Thus \(x+2=6\) or \(x+2=-6\), giving \(x=4\) or \(x=-8\). Choice A places the point 6 units from \(+2\), not from \(-2\). Choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Write the condition as an absolute value measured from -2, then consider moving 6 units in each direction from -2.

questions.title: Solving an Absolute-Value Equation Graphically
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The graph represents \(f(x)=|x-3|\). For which values of \(x\) does \(f(x)=5\)? Choose A or B, use the intersections shown by the graph, and verify them algebraically.
questions.explanation: The equation is \(|x-3|=5\), so \(x-3=5\) or \(x-3=-5\). These give \(x=8\) and \(x=-2\), respectively, matching the graph's two intersections. Choice B incorrectly treats the expression as if the distance were measured from zero instead of from 3. Choice A is correct.

visuals.alt: The V-shaped graph y equals absolute value of x minus 3 intersects the horizontal line y equals 5 at x equals minus 2 and x equals 8.

questions.hint: Read where the V-shaped graph meets the line y=5, then confirm by splitting the absolute value equation into its two cases.

questions.title: The Interval Around Negative Two
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Solve \(|x+2|<4\). Which interval contains every real solution and no other values? Choose A or B and explain why the endpoints are not included.
questions.explanation: The inequality \(|x+2|<4\) means that the distance between \(x\) and \(-2\) is less than 4. Therefore, \(-4<x+2<4\). Subtracting 2 throughout gives \(-6<x<2\). The endpoints give a distance of exactly 4, so they are excluded. Choice B shifts the interval in the wrong direction and is incorrect.
questions.hint: Rewrite the absolute value inequality as a double inequality and isolate x; decide whether equality is allowed.

questions.title: Distance Between Decimal Coordinates
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Point \(M\) is at \(-1.5\) and point \(N\) is at \(2.5\). What is the distance between the points? The table lists their coordinates. Choose A or B and justify the calculation.
questions.explanation: Distance is the absolute difference between the coordinates: \(|2.5-(-1.5)|=|4|=4\) units. Adding the coordinates, \(2.5+(-1.5)=1\), does not give the distance between the points. Therefore, choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: A table lists point M at minus 1.5 and point N at plus 2.5.

questions.hint: Subtract one coordinate from the other and take the absolute value; adding the coordinates does not measure distance.

questions.title: Where an Absolute-Value Graph Meets the Axis
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The graph is \(f(x)=|x-2|-3\). At which two values of \(x\) does the graph cross the horizontal axis? Choose A or B and show the equation you solve.
questions.explanation: The graph crosses the horizontal axis where \(f(x)=0\). Solve \(|x-2|-3=0\), giving \(|x-2|=3\). Thus \(x-2=3\) or \(x-2=-3\), so \(x=5\) or \(x=-1\). Choice B loses the negative sign when solving the second case. Choice A is correct.

visuals.alt: A V-shaped graph with vertex at (2, minus 3) crosses the horizontal axis at x equals minus 1 and x equals 5.

questions.hint: The graph crosses the horizontal axis where f(x)=0; write that equation and solve both cases of the absolute value.

questions.title: Solving for Two Coordinates from a Distance
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A real number \(x\) satisfies \(|2x-7|=9\). Which pair contains all solutions? Choose A or B and show both cases created by the absolute value.
questions.explanation: If \(|2x-7|=9\), then \(2x-7=9\) or \(2x-7=-9\). The first equation gives \(x=8\); the second gives \(2x=-2\), so \(x=-1\). Choice A loses the negative sign in the second solution. Choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Set the expression inside the absolute value equal to 9 and to -9, and solve each linear equation carefully.

questions.title: Equidistant from Two Expressions
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Find all real solutions to \(|2x-1|=|x+4|\). Choose A or B and justify why both sign cases must be considered.
questions.explanation: Two absolute values are equal when their inner expressions are equal or opposites. First, \(2x-1=x+4\), which gives \(x=5\). Second, \(2x-1=-(x+4)\), so \(3x=-3\) and \(x=-1\). Both values satisfy the original equation. Choice A comes from sign errors in these cases and is incorrect.
questions.hint: Two absolute values are equal when the expressions inside are equal or opposites; solve both equations.

questions.title: A Closed Interval from a Distance Bound
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The table gives the distance \(|x-4|\) for three values of \(x\). Find all real \(x\) satisfying \(|x-4|\le3\). Choose A or B, use the table as a check, and explain the full interval.
questions.explanation: The inequality \(|x-4|\le3\) means that \(x\) is no more than 3 units from 4. In symbols, \(-3\le x-4\le3\). Adding 4 gives \(1\le x\le7\). The table confirms that the endpoints are exactly 3 units from 4 and are included because the inequality allows equality. Choice B describes points outside the interval and is incorrect.

visuals.alt: A table shows that the distance from x to 4 is 3 at x equals 1, 0 at x equals 4, and 3 at x equals 7.

questions.hint: Rewrite the inequality as a double inequality around 4, and use the table to decide whether the endpoints belong.

questions.title: A Robot's Out-and-Back Route
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A robot starts at \(-4\) on a number line, moves 9 units to the right to \(+5\), and then moves 6 units to the left. How far is its final position from its starting position? Choose A or B and distinguish distance between the endpoints from the total distance traveled.
questions.explanation: After moving right, the robot is at \(-4+9=5\). Moving 6 units left puts it at \(5-6=-1\). The distance from the starting position to the final position is \(|-1-(-4)|=|3|=3\) units. The total route length is \(9+6=15\) units, which is not the distance between the endpoints. Therefore, choice B is correct.

visuals.alt: The robot's route starts at minus 4, reaches plus 5, and ends at minus 1; the starting and ending positions are 3 units apart.

questions.hint: Find the robot's final coordinate first, then compare it with the starting coordinate rather than adding the moves.

questions.title: The Thermometer's Final Reading
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A thermometer reads \(-3^\circ\text{C}\). The temperature rises by \(8^\circ\text{C}\) and later falls by \(5^\circ\text{C}\). What is the final reading? Choose A or B and track the signed changes in order.
questions.explanation: After the rise, the temperature is \(-3+8=5^\circ\text{C}\). After the fall, it is \(5-5=0^\circ\text{C}\). The value \(3\) is the net change, \(8-5\), and not the final reading; the starting temperature was already \(-3^\circ\text{C}\). Choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Apply the changes in order as signed numbers: a rise adds and a fall subtracts.

questions.title: Intersecting Two Absolute-Value Conditions
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: How many integers satisfy both \(|x-2|\le4\) and \(|x+1|>2\)? Choose A or B and show how you combine the two conditions rather than counting each condition separately.
questions.explanation: The first condition gives \(-4\le x-2\le4\), so \(-2\le x\le6\). The second gives \(x+1>2\) or \(x+1<-2\), which means \(x>1\) or \(x<-3\). Within \([-2,6]\), only the values \(x>1\) remain. The integers are \(2,3,4,5,6\), for a total of 5. Choice B counts the integers in the first interval without applying the second condition, so it is incorrect.
questions.hint: Solve each inequality as intervals on the number line, then keep only the integers that lie in both.

questions.title: A Sum of Distances from Two Fixed Points
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For which values of \(x\) does \(|x-1|+|x+1|=6\)? Choose A or B and explain how the answer depends on whether \(x\) lies between \(-1\) and \(1\) or outside that interval.
questions.explanation: The expression is the sum of the distances from \(x\) to \(1\) and to \(-1\). If \(-1\le x\le1\), those distances add to 2, so the sum cannot be 6 there. For \(x>1\), the sum is \((x-1)+(x+1)=2x\), which equals 6 at \(x=3\). For \(x<-1\), the sum is \((1-x)+(-x-1)=-2x\), which equals 6 at \(x=-3\). Choice A gives a sum of 4, not 6. Choice B is correct.
questions.hint: Interpret the sum as distances to 1 and to -1, and check the region between them separately from the regions outside.

questions.title: Comparing Two Absolute-Value Functions
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The graphs of \(y=|2x-4|\) and \(y=|x+2|\) are shown. For which real values of \(x\) is \(|2x-4|\le|x+2|\)? Choose A or B, use the intersection points, and verify the interval algebraically.
questions.explanation: Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring preserves the inequality: \((2x-4)^2\le(x+2)^2\). Expanding and collecting terms gives \(3x^2-20x+12\le0\), which factors as \((3x-2)(x-6)\le0\). Since the quadratic opens upward, it is nonpositive between its roots, \(x=\frac23\) and \(x=6\), inclusive. This agrees with the graph. Choice A has the wrong sign on the lower endpoint and is incorrect.

visuals.alt: The V-shaped graphs y equals absolute value of 2x minus 4 and y equals absolute value of x plus 2 intersect at x equals two thirds and x equals 6; the first graph is no higher between the intersections.

questions.hint: Find where the two V-graphs intersect (or square both nonnegative sides), then decide between which points the first graph is lower.

questions.title: A Parameter That Controls the Number of Solutions
questions.learningObjective: Apply number lines and distance and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For which real values of the parameter \(k\) does the equation \(|x-4|=kx\) have exactly two distinct real solutions for \(x\)? Choose A or B and analyze the possible cases, including the boundary values.
questions.explanation:
When \(0<k<1\), the branch \(x<4\) gives \(4-x=kx\), so \(x=\frac4{k+1}\), which lies between 0 and 4. The branch \(x\ge4\) gives \(x-4=kx\), so \(x=\frac4{1-k}\), which is at least 4. These are two distinct valid solutions.

At \(k=0\), the equation has only \(x=4\). At \(k=1\), the branch \(x\ge4\) has no solution and the other branch gives only \(x=2\). For \(k<0\), the requirement \(kx\ge0\) forces \(x\le0\); there can be at most one solution on that region. For \(k>1\), the branch \(x\ge4\) has no solution and the branch \(x<4\) gives at most one. Thus exactly two distinct solutions occur precisely when \(0<k<1\). Choice B incorrectly includes the endpoint values, so choice A is correct.
questions.hint: Split the absolute value into the cases x<4 and x>=4, solve each for x in terms of k, and check when each solution really lies in its case.
